subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core ACP skill-context injection contract for `sessions_spawn`, and which explicit, automatic, or default selection modes plus prompt and audit semantics are allowed?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the request changes cross-runtime prompt authority, security redaction, and session observability in ways automation should not choose for maintainers.

options.title: Design the core ACP contract first
options.body: Specify the selection modes, prompt layer, redaction/audit metadata, resume behavior, and Codex-native interaction, then implement the bounded code path.

options.title: Limit to existing agent skill filters
options.body: Keep spawn-time ACP injection out of core for now and document that users should configure skill availability at the agent level instead.

options.title: Decline core injection
options.body: Close this as unsupported if maintainers want ACP harnesses to rely only on their native skill systems and manual prompt context.

recommendation.title: Design the core ACP contract first
recommendation.body: Specify the selection modes, prompt layer, redaction/audit metadata, resume behavior, and Codex-native interaction, then implement the bounded code path.

likelyOwner.reason: The central implementation and product contract sit on the ACP `sessions_spawn` path introduced in PR #23580.
